ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:

Abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is important in human-machine interactions, enabling machines to detect and classify human emotions from solely human speech. Speech emotion recognition (SER) benchmarks routinely report accuracies above 90 percent, yet these models fail when deployed or tested on diverse speakers. The papers overlook a fundamental issue: models may be learning speaker identity and tone rather than generalized emotional cues. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: ADReasoner: Acoustic-Linguistic Cue-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Explainable Alzheimer's Disease Detection from Speech
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.34220v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech-based Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection holds significant promise due to its scalable and non-invasive nature. However, current Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs), similar to conventional AD detection systems, still treat AD detection primarily as a simple categorical classification task. This paradigm provides limited interpretability of predictions, while leaving the inherent expressiveness and reasoning capabilities of SpeechLLMs largely underutilized. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.34401v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial audio is central to immersive 360$^\circ$ media, yet existing audio-visual spatialization renders the scene as a whole, leaving no control over an individual source. We introduce Audio-Visual Query-conditioned Target Sound Spatialization (AV-QTSS): given a monaural multi-source mixture, a 360$^\circ$ video and a class query from the 13-class DCASE sound-event ontology, it generates the first-order Ambisonics (FOA) signal of the queried source alone. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.34413v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large audio language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance on standard speech and audio understanding tasks, yet their ability to systematically generalize to novel task compositions remains underexplored. Taking a meta-learning view, we extend Text-to-LoRA (T2L) to LALMs, generating instruction-conditioned LoRA adapters with a Transformer hypernetwork rather than learning a single fixed adapter shared across instructions. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.34814v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discrete-token-based universal speech enhancement (USE) enables strong sequence modeling but often suffers from a quality--fidelity trade-off, where perceptually plausible outputs may alter linguistic content or speaker characteristics. We present TIMUSE, a two-stage USE framework combining text-initialized masked semantic restoration with acoustic reconstruction. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.35144v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hardware-aware training often optimizes FPGA resources, latency, or bit operations, but folding changes what compression saves: shared arithmetic decouples precision, weight storage, and scheduled work. We derive training objectives from the measured costs of a folded streaming speech-enhancement accelerator. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.35581v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A full-duplex spoken dialogue model must yield when the user cuts in and hold when the user merely backchannels. Sequence-level RL with a timing reward (GRPO) is the usual recipe; we test its whole-rollout form on four open models and find two failures. A binary window reward gives zero advantage on exactly the windows that most need learning (a zero-gradient trap), and the one score per rollout is spread over listening-state decisions the reward is not written in terms of (credit leakage), so the model talks into silence or stops answering. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: A Robust, Explainable, and Efficient Deep Metric for Speech and General Audio Quality
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.35810v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a robust Speech and Audio Quality Metric (SAQM) that merges features of traditional quality metrics with a CNN trained on a large amount of data using contrastive learning methods. To overcome the problem of limited amounts of human-labeled training data, we propose two pretraining strategies relying on pseudo-labels. One uses an established objective metric PEAQ-2f (based on ITU-R BS.1387) as surrogate loss, the other is based on contrasting a wide range of coding modes by a rule-of-thumb ordering based on expected perceived quality.

Abstract: Speaking-style captioning (SSC) aims to generate natural language descriptions of how speech is delivered, capturing paralinguistic attributes such as vocal timbre, prosody, and expressivity. Many downstream applications, including conversational AI agents, controllable speech generation, and large-scale audio annotation, require dimension-specific style captions that describe targeted aspects of speech (e.g., speaker traits, emotion, or delivery style), rather than a single undifferentiated description. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.33127v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Active speaker detection (ASD) relies on audiovisual correspondence between speech and visible faces, yet this correspondence becomes unreliable in crowded scenes, or when visual evidence is unavailable. arXiv:2610.33434v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic DJ systems mostly target electronic dance music, whose regular structure makes rule-based mixing relatively easier. Vocal-rich popular music is harder: which track to play next, where to cue it, and which transition to use are tied together, so fixed rules handle them poorly. We present DJustify, a pop AI-DJ that puts an LLM in a reason--propose--verify--repair loop and lets it choose the next track, cue points, and mixing technique together. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.33974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sperm-whale codas are usually described by the number and timing of their clicks. Earlier acoustic studies showed that individual clicks and longer coda sequences contain additional organization. We ask how that organization compares with music, whose smaller sounds also form larger units and ordered sequences. We compare codas with performed violin music, drum grooves, and sung melodies. arXiv:2610.34156v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing anti-spoofing systems report either an utterance-level score or a time-based spoof interval: the former cannot show which words are spoofed, while the latter does not directly match the transcript and must be post-aligned with words, so alignment errors can lead to wrong word-level labels. arXiv:2610.34183v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learning audio representations that effectively bridge holistic global soundscapes with fine-grained acoustic moments is a long-standing goal in self-supervised learning. Recording-level contrastive objectives encourage agreement between pooled audio representations, but do not explicitly supervise local time-frequency representations. Abstract: Symbolic music representations encode musical content at varying levels of completeness, from performance-oriented formats such as MIDI to fully notated scores such as MusicXML. Yet the impact of this representational richness on deep learning models remains poorly understood. Abstract: While recent advances in text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis have substantially improved speech quality and modeling flexibility, the development of lightweight and computationally efficient systems remains comparatively underexplored. Abstract: Spatial audio authoring coordinates source decisions with soundfield synthesis. For editing, plans specify what to change and retain, while reference audio supplies further acoustic detail. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.34533v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pretrained audio spectrogram transformers are widely used as backbones of machine listening systems for sound event classification. However, they are typically trained using spectrograms with a fixed Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) configuration, implicitly binding the model to the time-frequency resolution seen during pretraining. Abstract: Reasoning is increasingly important for large audio-language models (LALMs), yet remains relatively underexplored compared with text-only and vision-language models. We introduce Audio-R1, a reinforcement learning (RL) post-training framework that revisits audio self-supervised learning as a source of verifiable rewards for improving audio understanding and reasoning task performance. CDM — Create Digital Music.title: On the sublime BETHLEHEM بيت لحم, walls in time and space fall
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
The exquisite collaboration of Lawrence Sammour, Sary Moussa, and Abed Kobeissy, Bethlehem, is released this month. And it has become a rich sanctuary, a shared space that refuses erasure or fragmentation. It also refuses to obey the boundaries of colonialism and occupation, weaving together what was pulled apart, as taut and resonant as the strings of the buzuq.

Roland has one more announcement -- a 1.5 update for its flagship TR-1000 drum machine. That includes note sequencing, a must-requested keyboard mode for playing bass and melodic parts on the gear, the ability to swap patterns and kits with effects on without a hitch, and a lot of tweaks and UI improvements.

The post Roland TR-1000 1.5: keyboard mode, seamless kit switching, more appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: The world is your modular: Mulch Box, an all-jacks patch bay and multiplier
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
It's the size of a standard guitar pedal. It needs no power It's... covered in jacks. It's Mulch Box, the first hardware from Go Outside, and it's a stunningly simple idea for signal routing any of your gear, minijack and full-sized jack alike.

The post The world is your modular: Mulch Box, an all-jacks patch bay and multiplier appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Arturia’s new MiniFreak 49 synth is tactile, exploration-friendly: tested
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
It's not just some extra keys or minor feature tweaks. Arturia's MiniFreak 49 has evolved the range into a synthesizer you can freely explore just by playing, not programming. It's a fusion of tactile experience and sound, right when we need that. Here's a full hands-on test.

The post Arturia’s new MiniFreak 49 synth is tactile, exploration-friendly: tested appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Baby Roland is back: Boutique JUPITER-08, n/vision wavetable synths
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
The kawaii look of the mini Rolands in the Boutique series has returned. There's one vintage remake -- the JUPITER-08, this time with full polyphony and then some (up to 32 voices). And there's something new: the n/vision wavetable synth.

The post Baby Roland is back: Boutique JUPITER-08, n/vision wavetable synths appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Abed Eyad is making beats in Gaza: interview, call for support
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
20-year-old Palestinian producer Abed Eyad is making beats from the rubble, surviving amidst genocide. He talks to us about what that's like, what drives his productions, and how to support his music.

The post Abed Eyad is making beats in Gaza: interview, call for support appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.
